turns.assessment: The simultaneous OTU_LOF events, large ~72–74 ps DGD increases, and BER degradation across multiple independent channels indicate a common optical-path PMD event, not a client-port, OTN-switch, or individual transponder failure. Stable receive power, OSNR, channel-monitor readings, and amplifier telemetry strongly oppose cuts, connector faults, amplifier failures, and WSS attenuation faults. The evidence supports DGD_RISE on a shared upstream fibre span, but end-to-end DGD measurements do not identify which individual span, so no repair location reaches the 80% commitment threshold.

proposals.rationale: All six affected line receivers show nearly simultaneous OTU_LOF, large DGD increases, and BER deterioration while optical power and OSNR remain unchanged. That is the characteristic signature of excessive DGD on a fibre span common to the affected optical paths, but the available receiver measurements cannot localize the responsible span.

A polarization transient could correlate errors across channels without changing power, particularly on an aerial span, but it is normally millisecond-scale and would not explain the sustained LOF and 300 errored seconds as well as DGD_RISE.
